facts.value: The counters form a repeating measurement window. vr_count advances once per pre-retrace callback, while renew_count advances at most once in that callback when a new presentation is staged. Reaching frame_period atomically publishes the accumulated renewal count and resets both values to zero; before that threshold, both values persist unchanged except for their applicable increments. HSD_VIInit resets perf.frame_renew but does not reset these function-local statics, so repeated initialization does not start a fresh counter window.
facts.rationale: Correct inherited claim using pinned source and recorded object observations.

facts.value: Signature: `void HSD_VICopyEFB2XFBPtr(HSD_VIStatus* vi, void* buffer, HSD_RenderPass rpass)`. `vi` supplies the render mode and copy/filter/clear/update configuration, `buffer` is the base address of destination XFB storage, and `rpass` is an enum-like domain accepting `HSD_RP_SCREEN`, `HSD_RP_TOPHALF`, or `HSD_RP_BOTTOMHALF`. Other enum values, including HSD_RP_OFFSCREEN, reach panic. Pointers, dimensions, destination capacity and overlap constraints are unchecked locally; split geometry assumes efbHeight is at least four and scratch width fits its fixed 640-pixel allocation.

facts.value: Fewer than two XFBs is inert. Otherwise waits for a drawable slot, submits a copy, snapshots current settings into the slot while changing DRAWING to WAITDONE, waits for any prior GX fence and arms a new fence with the slot index. The internal GX callback only clears its waiting flag and invokes an optional registered callback. Progress from WAITDONE requires that callback or other external code to call HSD_VIDrawDoneXFB; initialization leaves the user callback NULL, so completion alone does not ensure queue progress.
facts.rationale: Correct inherited claim using pinned source and recorded object observations.

facts.value: A non-NULL argument enables or replaces the optional post-retrace user hook, while `NULL` disables it. facts.value: Returns immediately when fewer than two XFBs are configured. Otherwise it remains in a wait-and-recheck state while at least one XFB is WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, or NEXT, sleeping through one or more retraces so draw-done and retrace callbacks can advance the presentation state. It exits as soon as an interrupt-protected snapshot finds none of those three statuses; DISPLAY and other statuses do not by themselves keep this flush active. No timeout or cancellation exists; queue drainage depends on interrupt/callback progress, including an external draw-done callback that advances WAITDONE.
facts.rationale: Correct inherited claim using pinned source and recorded object observations.

facts.value: If fewer than two XFBs are configured, the function returns immediately. Otherwise it remains in a tight polling loop while any XFB is WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, or NEXT and exits only when none has those statuses. Unlike HSD_VIWaitXFBFlush, it performs no VIWaitForRetrace call between polls and therefore does not voluntarily yield while waiting. No timeout exists. Each poll restores the incoming interrupt state; a caller entering with interrupts disabled does not gain progress merely from the temporary disable/restore sequence.

facts.value: The unit maintains a presentation state machine around one EFB and up to three XFB slots. Configured XFB slots initialize as FREE and absent slots as NONE, while the EFB initializes as FREE. An asynchronous copy advances a selected XFB through DRAWING and WAITDONE; draw completion changes WAITDONE to NEXT when no frame is already queued, or to DRAWDONE when a NEXT frame exists. At post-retrace, DISPLAY becomes FREE, NEXT becomes DISPLAY, and any DRAWDONE frame advances to NEXT. The draw-done callback state separately tracks whether a GX completion is pending and the integer argument forwarded to its registered callback. WAITDONE advancement requires external registration or invocation of HSD_VIDrawDoneXFB; the internal GX callback does not perform that transition itself and initialization leaves its user callback NULL.
facts.rationale: Correct inherited claim using pinned source and recorded object observations.
